Thanks David — available and on it. Initial notes from our side (so Nova's reviewers have context):

Summary (short):
- Private deployment: customer operates a peered VPC or on-prem connector. Control plane signals (management API, audit logs) are mediated by a Redwood control plane endpoint located in the customer VPC for fully private installs; for VPC-with-peering we terminate management in a customer-managed subnet and keep the data plane flows strictly over private interconnects.
- Dedicated (hosted reserved capacity): compute sits in Redwood-managed subnets but each customer gets isolated tenant pools. Control plane is reachable only over mutual TLS with customer-authenticated certificates; kernel-level tenancy plus security groups and microsegmentation prevent cross-tenant lateral traffic.

What we'll include in the package (attached):
- network-annotated-map-v1.png — single-page diagram showing control/data/telemetry paths and which segments are customer-owned vs Redwood-managed.
- private-dedicated-isolation-matrix.xlsx — mapping of traffic flows to controls and CAIQ/SIG identifiers. Columns: Flow, Source, Destination, Plane, Encryption, ACLs/Policies, CAIQ refs.
- caiq-reference-index.pdf — short narrative mapping key Redwood controls to CAIQ/typical SOC 2 items (network and access subsections).

Quick clarifications for Nova's intake team:
- Telemetry/metrics: aggregated telemetry is forwarded over an encrypted channel to Redwood telemetry collectors; for Private with air-gapped installs we can optionally push telemetry to a customer-managed collector instead. We'll mark both options in the index.
- Egress: default Dedicated behaviour is deny-by-default for outbound to the public internet; explicit egress routes for model downloads are documented in the matrix.

I'll attach the items and flag specific CAIQ IDs in the XLS. If Nova wants a short walkthrough, propose Thu or Fri afternoon PT.

Alice — quick answers inline and noted in the matrix (see attached cells):

1) Dedicated tenant vNICs: isolation is enforced at multiple layers. We use SR-IOV on supported hardware for high-throughput tenants to reduce software shared planes where applicable; on general-purpose pools we use per-tenant MAC/VLAN assignment and strict microsegmentation in the hypervisor NIC stack. In the isolation matrix we mark flows where SR-IOV is present vs software isolation and provide the firmware/driver references.

2) Control-plane endpoints: for Private peered-VPC installs control endpoints are private IPs only (no public control-plane endpoint). For Private hosted-with-fallback (some customers opt for hybrid), we publish a customer-specific public endpoint that is locked down with mTLS + customer IP allowlists — that mode is documented as an opt-in fallback in the XLS.

We'll walk through the matrix on Thu 2026-10-21 15:00 PT. I've attached the three artifacts mentioned in Kim's email to this thread. If you need additional low-level firmware proofs or attestations (driver versions, SR-IOV capability reports), flag it in the call and we can prepare a short addendum.
